title: fix(post): a milling operation is never posted on a lathe's work spindle
body:
## What changed

A lathe post opens every section that states no C angle with the WORK spindle (`G97 S M03`). The stream names no operation family, so a milling pass that stays on one meridian read to `fanuc-lathe.cps` and `tormach-lathe.cps` exactly like a turning pass, and posted the work spindle at the cutter's rpm with the cutter standing still.

The program gate now decides it before a line is written, from what it already holds (the operation's kind, its cached path, its work offset). Through a turning dialect a section passes only as live-tool work (its path states C), a turning-family kind, or a Drill whose every cutting move and cycle is on the spindle axis with the tool along +Z. Every other operation is refused by name.

- `crates/app/src/lathe_voice.rs` (new): `voice(params, path, origin) -> LatheVoice { WorkSpindle, LiveTool, Refused(why) }` is the one derivation; `voice_of(world, entity)` reads it from the document; `at_post(world, ops, cps)` is the door.
- The door is called where a script is known: `post_script_body` (so `post_script`, `post_setup`, one-mount `post_mounts`), `post_each` (several mounts, each with its own script) and `post_per_op_with`. It runs before the verification report in all three, so the user reads this refusal first.
- `crates/post/src/post/dialect.rs` (new): `speaks_turning(cps)` reads the script's own manifest (`capabilities`, the mask every shipped post already states: 2 for the two lathe posts, 1 for the rest); `states_live_tool(path)` is the one "does the path state C?" test, and the stream's `PARAM LiveTool` is now written from it.
- No change to the stream format, the CL spec or any post script. A mill post is untouched: there `M03` is the cutter's own spindle.

## Reproductions (both re-verified on main before the fix)

Mill-turn bench (spindle as C, live-tool words stated, spindle maximum 15000 so the machine's rpm limit masks nothing), through `fanuc-lathe.cps`.

**(a) Drill DR-0400, one hole at X0 Y0** - correct voicing, unchanged, still posts:

```
G97 S10000 M03
M8
G00 X0 Z20
G83 Z10 Q12000 F0.008
```

**(b) Face, flat end mill EM-0400-2FL, one pass along Y = 0** - before, no refusal from either lathe script:

```
(OPERATION: F1 - FACE - G54)
G54
(T0202 EM-0400-2FL - FLAT END MILL D4)
T0202
G50 S15000
G97 S12000 M03
M8
G00 X-24 Z30
G01 X-24 Z4 F0.0083
G01 X24 Z4 F0.025
```

After, from every post entry point, nothing written:

```
F1: a Face operation would be posted on the work spindle - a lathe post turns the work at the tool's speed while the cutter stands still, so nothing is milled; cut it as C-axis live tooling (a rotary operation), or move it to a setup that posts through a mill post, or suppress the operation
```

Through `fanuc.cps` the same document posts as before.

## Per-kind table (all 41 kinds, on a path that stays on the meridian and on one that stays on the axis)

| Kinds | Through a lathe post |
|---|---|
| Turning family (12): Facing, Profile Rough, Profile Finish, Groove Rough, Groove Finish, Parting, Threading, Chamfering, Taper Turning, Multi-Pass Turning, Form Turning, Boring | posts on the work spindle |
| Any kind whose path states C (in practice Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset on the spindle's C) | posts with the live-tool voicing |
| Drill, every cutting move and cycle on the spindle axis, tool along +Z (drill, centre drill, tap cycle, reamer) | posts on the work spindle, as (a) |
| Drill with a hole off the axis (on the meridian or not), or a tilted (cross) drill | refused, naming the hole: `D2: a Drill operation would be posted on the work spindle with a hole off the spindle axis (X6.000 Y0.000 from the work offset) - ...` |
| Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, Slot, Trace, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Engrave, 2D Chamfer, Circular, Thread (thread mill), Bore (helical), Trochoidal slot, 3D Pocket, 3D Finish, Deburr, 5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour, and the three rotary kinds when their path states no C | refused by name, on the meridian and on centre |
| Probe | refused by name ("cannot be posted through a lathe post - it would open the section on the work spindle and writes no probing") |
| Plasma Profile | refused by name |

Decided one by one: a tap on centre is a Drill with the tap cycle and is admitted (the work turns, the tap stands still - lathe practice); Bore is refused (its cutter orbits the hole); the thread-mill Thread is refused (the cutter must turn). On-centre is exact because tool and work then share one axis, so it makes no difference to the cut which of the two turns; off the axis that is gone. Tolerance: `spindle_law::SPINDLE_TOL`, 0.0005 mm, the lathe scripts' own `EPS`. Rapids are not judged.

## The route, and why

The smaller route: a law at the program gate, no stream parameter. The gate already holds everything the law needs, so the refusal is made before the stream exists; a stream parameter would only let the *script* say the same thing, at the cost of a format change and goldens moving in every dialect. No case defeated the smaller route. The parameter becomes worth it when a lathe post should *voice* a milling section with a driven tool and no C move (new behaviour, not this fix). Recorded in `docs/decisions/1190-mill-op-on-lathe-post.md`.

## The shared predicate (for PR #1191)

"Is this section voiced on the work spindle?" is `camcraft_app::lathe_voice::on_work_spindle(world, &entity)`, and the full answer is `lathe_voice::voice_of(world, &entity) -> Option<LatheVoice>`: `WorkSpindle` is the section whose stated rpm turns the work, `LiveTool` the one whose work turns on C, `Refused` one that never reaches a lathe post. `setup_workholding::work_speed` can map those three onto its `Stated` / `OnC` / `Not` instead of keeping its own reading. One difference it would pick up: a mill-turn's on-centre Drill is `WorkSpindle` here, and today's `spindle_law::turns` leaves it out, so it is not held to the chuck limit. `setup_workholding.rs` is not touched by this PR.

## Entry points

GUI Post (`posting::post_mounts`), GUI Post per operation (`posting::post_per_op`), the script verb and the MCP `post` tool (`api::v_post` -> `post_mounts` / `post_mounts_script`), and the CLI through those. All go through `op_streams` and then one of the three bodies that hold the script. `posting::stream_records` (the gate-free stream the test suites hand to `engine::run`) is not gated: it holds no script.

## Goldens

Byte-identical; no golden file is in the diff. The lathe goldens hold only Drill (three, all on X0), Facing, Groove Finish, Parting, Profile Rough, Profile Finish and Threading sections, plus two synthetic C-axis streams: no mill-family section on the work spindle, so nothing to list as a finding.

## Pinning tests

- `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name` (the table over `KindInfo::ALL`; the expectation is an exhaustive match, so a new kind does not compile until it is decided)
- `lathe_voice::tests::a_drill_is_admitted_only_with_every_cut_on_the_spindle_axis_along_z`
- `lathe_voice::tests::the_door_refuses_on_every_turning_dialect_and_passes_every_milling_one` (every kind against every built-in post; registry list and manifests agree)
- `lathe_work_spindle::a_drill_on_centre_posts_on_the_work_spindle_as_a_lathe_drills` (reproduction a)
- `lathe_work_spindle::a_face_pass_on_the_meridian_is_refused_by_name_never_posted_on_the_work_spindle` (reproduction b, both lathe dialects)
- `lathe_work_spindle::every_post_entry_point_refuses_it` (`post_script`, `post_setup`, `post_mounts`, `post_mounts_script`, `post_per_op`, `post_per_op_script`, MCP `post` with and without a named post)
- `lathe_work_spindle::a_drill_off_centre_on_the_meridian_is_refused_by_name`
- `lathe_work_spindle::live_tool_and_turning_sections_pass_the_lathe_door`
- `post::dialect::tests::the_turning_bit_is_read_from_the_manifest_mask`, `a_path_is_live_tool_work_only_when_a_move_states_c`

## How tested

On the final head `50c0bea7` (the fix `ee8423cd` plus a merge of `origin/main` at `d7e9a807`, which had moved under the branch):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the first run - post suites (19 binaries) and app suites (the lib plus 125 suites it mapped from `app::posting` / `post::post`), 1259 tests passed, 0 failed, 8.0 min wall.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Before the merge, on `ee8423cd`: `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all green) and the app suites `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_refusals`, `lathe_workholding_rpm`, `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`, `edm_machine`, `conformance`, `operations` (117), `golden_cl` (25), `solid_law_goldens`, plus every other suite that posts through a lathe dialect at the real gate (`lathe_cross_drill`, `drilling_axial`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_holder`, `drilling_cross_stock`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `per_op_files`, `post_not_judged`, `setup_mount`, `setup_mounts_post`, `coolant_followups`): all green, no existing assertion changed.

## Not exercised

- Not run on a real control.
- The five candidates the issue listed beyond Face and Drill (a 2D contour in the ZX plane, an engrave on centre, a thread mill, a Bore on centre, a probe) are proved at the law and the door with hand-built meridian and on-axis paths for every kind, not with paths from their real generators. The law is by kind for them, so the path's shape does not enter.
- A C-axis section and a turning pass are shown to pass the door and to be voiced correctly by the script, but neither bench posts end to end through `post_script`: the verifier holds both for reasons of their fixtures (rapid-in-stock warnings, a finish-envelope warning), unrelated to this change.
- A user's own lathe script that declares no `capabilities` is not recognised as a turning dialect, so the door does not fire for it. Filed as #1199.
- The mirror case, a turning-family operation through a mill post, was not examined.
- UI suites were not run (no UI code changed; the GUI calls `post_mounts` / `post_per_op`).

Changelog: A milling operation on a mill-turn is no longer posted on the work spindle by a lathe post: through a lathe post only turning operations, C-axis live-tool sections and on-centre Drill holes post, and every other operation is refused by name

Effort: max (escalated once from high by the first worker; no escalation in this run)

Fixes #1190
